q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most: 36% of their videos outperformed their baseline (n=89 videos), versus 22% for mid-size channels (n=50) and 5.3% for large channels (n=38). Average relative lift follows the same order: about 8.0x for small, 3.7x for mid, 1.3x for large.

Audiences are mostly lukewarm. Net sentiment on product-side comments is slightly positive for small channels (+0.061, n=2,714 comments) and a bit better for mid (+0.109, n=2,335). Large channels are slightly negative (-0.025, n=1,965), with more negative (38.8%) than positive (36.2%) comments.

So mid-size channels pair decent breakout rates with the happiest audiences, while large channels do worst on both measures. Caveat: these are associations from a comment sample, not causes, and the large group has the fewest videos.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'nano%' OR cr.tier LIKE 'micro%' THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'mid%' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier LIKE 'macro%' OR cr.tier LIKE 'mega%' THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), vid AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM base WHERE outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size_group), com AS (SELECT b.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)-AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN base b ON b.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY b.size_group) SELECT v.size_group, v.n_videos_with_baseline, v.outperformer_rate, v.avg_rel_lift, c.n_product_side, c.pct_positive, c.pct_negative, CASE WHEN c.n_product_side>=10 THEN c.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment FROM vid v LEFT JOIN com c ON c.size_group=v.size_group ORDER BY v.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions looks like the best-supported format for mid-sized channels. It has the largest sample (n=19 videos), and 42% of those videos outperformed their baseline. Mean relative lift was 2.7, and net sentiment was positive at +0.23 (n=1,028 product-side comments).

Full review and durability test both show a 100% outperformer rate, but each is a single video, so I wouldn't draw conclusions from them.

Explainer/tips (n=8) is mixed. Only 12.5% outperformed, yet mean lift was 9.7, which suggests one or two big hits are skewing the average. Sentiment was slightly negative (-0.06).

Comparison (n=6), upgrade advice (n=8), meme shorts (n=4) and keynote recaps (n=2) had no outperformers.

Caveat: these are associations, not causes, and most formats have small samples.
sql: WITH vids AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), perf AS (SELECT format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift FROM vids GROUP BY format), sent AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_neg FROM vids v JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=v.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT perf.format, perf.n_videos, perf.n_with_baseline, perf.outperformer_rate, perf.mean_rel_lift, sent.n_product_side, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN ROUND(sent.pct_pos - sent.pct_neg,3) END AS net_sentiment FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.format=perf.format ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC, perf.mean_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
Two high-lift videos stand out for the most negative reaction. "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" (Time Travel Visuals) has a lift of 499.28 (rel_lift 72.9) on 20.5M views. Among product-side comments (n=76), about 70% were negative and 11% positive, so net sentiment is -0.59. "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" (TechDroider) has a lift of 86.8 (rel_lift 12.7) on 2.0M views. Among product-side comments (n=56), about 70% were negative and 18% positive, so net sentiment is -0.52.

Lift and sentiment are separate measures here. Both videos spread widely, and the reaction under them is mostly critical.

Caveat: these are sampled comments, with n of 56 to 76 per video, and the result shows associations, not causes.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(sentiment='positive') AS pct_pos, AVG(sentiment='negative') AS pct_neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT ct.video_id, ct.title, cr.name AS creator, ct.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pct_pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.pct_neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pct_pos - s.pct_neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content ct JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id = ct.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id = ct.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id = ct.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Largest topics by total comments: "Samsung Did It First" (n=820), praise for review quality (n=543), price complaints (n=478), Apple ad parody humor (n=466), and "Eager to Buy" (n=461).

Fastest growing this week versus last, among topics with prior-week n of at least 10:
- Left-handed concerns: 89 vs 13, about +585%
- "Waiting for Next Year": 51 vs 10, +410%
- Wanting pro cameras: 38 vs 11, +246%
- Apple ad parody humor: 113 vs 37, +205%
- Under-display camera: 95 vs 32, +197%

By raw added comments, "Samsung Did It First" gained the most (+128, to 210), followed by "Eager to Buy" (+99).

Caveat: the top percentage gains start from small bases (prior n of 10 to 13), so they can swing a lot. Several other topics had too little prior-week data to show growth.
sql: WITH mx AS (SELECT max(day_since_launch) AS d FROM comments), c AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.day_since_launch AS dsl FROM comments cm JOIN content v ON v.video_id = cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, count(*) AS n_total, sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week, sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abs_change, CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 10 THEN round(1.0*(sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl > mx.d-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / sum(CASE WHEN c.dsl <= mx.d-7 AND c.dsl > mx.d-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 3) END AS wow_growth, mx.d AS latest_day FROM c JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = c.topic_id CROSS JOIN mx GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, mx.d ORDER BY n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Most-liked: Samsung comparisons and buying interest. Most-criticised: price and durability. But the same topics show up on both sides, so these are really the main debates rather than clear likes or dislikes.

Liked (positive comments, out of 6,104 product comments):
- "Samsung Did It First" had 320 positive comments (5.2% of all comments).
- "Eager to Buy" had 212, and 46% of its comments were positive (n=461).
- "Samsung Fold Comparisons" had 200, and 48% were positive (n=417).

Criticised (negative comments):
- "Samsung Did It First" had 324 negative comments.
- Price complaints had 197 (n=478, 41% negative).
- Durability doubts had 179 (n=452, 40%).
- The under-display camera had 124 (n=299, 42%).

Caveat: these are sampled comments, and the sentiment labels are imperfect. Positive and negative counts for most topics are close, so treat the ranking as indicative only.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.sentiment, t.topic_id, t.name FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND t.pool='product'), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM base GROUP BY topic_id, name), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_n FROM base) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, name AS topic, n AS topic_n, pos AS side_n, ROUND(pos*1.0/n,3) AS share_of_topic, ROUND(pos*1.0/total_n,3) AS share_of_all_product_comments, total_n FROM agg, tot ORDER BY pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, n, neg, ROUND(neg*1.0/n,3), ROUND(neg*1.0/total_n,3), total_n FROM agg, tot ORDER BY neg DESC LIMIT 8)
